    Environment and rewards¶

    autoqec_sim.env ¶

    Batched code-discovery environment with gymnasium-style semantics.

    The state is one batched tableau of shape (batch, 2n, 2n + 1); every batch element is an independent episode. Actions are Clifford gates: the single-qubit gates on every qubit and the two-qubit gates on both orientations of every edge of a connectivity graph. The reward is any callable f(tab, k) -> (batch,), by default the Knill-Laflamme reward of autoqec_sim.reward. There is no dependency on gymnasium; reset and step follow its calling convention (observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info).

    An optional LDPC constraint (ldpc_w_max) restricts the search to states whose stabilizer group has a generating set with every generator of weight at most w_max (autoqec_sim.ldpc.ldpc_feasible, exact for n - k <= 14). Mode "terminate" ends the episode of an element that leaves the feasible set with ldpc_violation_reward; mode "mask" reverts such an action to a no-op (the step is still counted) and CodeDiscoveryEnv.feasible_action_mask gives agents the full per-action mask; mode "final" leaves the path free and only withholds success from an infeasible state (the constraint binds the solution, not the trajectory). A soft alternative is the reward term autoqec_sim.ldpc.make_ldpc_penalty. terminated is true when an episode ends by success or by violation; info["success"] distinguishes them.

    autoqec_sim.reward ¶

    Knill-Laflamme rewards, vectorized over a batch of tableaux.

    Following Olle et al. (arXiv:2311.04750, Eq. 10), an error E_mu is detected by the code with stabilizer group S if it anticommutes with some stabilizer generator or lies in S (a degenerate error acts trivially). K_mu = 0 in that case and 1 otherwise, and the reward is r = -sum_mu lam_mu K_mu. Detecting every Pauli of weight < d is equivalent to the Knill-Laflamme conditions for correcting all errors of weight at most (d - 1) // 2, since the conditions involve products E_a^dagger E_b of two such errors.

    Membership in S is decided without linear algebra: a Pauli that commutes with all n - k stabilizer generators lies in the normalizer, and it lies in S iff it also commutes with all 2k logical operators, because the logicals form a symplectic basis of N(S) / S. So K_mu = 1 iff E_mu commutes with every stabilizer row and anticommutes with at least one logical row. Both tests are one batched symplectic product of the error set against the n + k relevant rows of the tableau.

    CompositeReward ¶

    Weighted sum of reward callables f(tab, k) -> (batch,).

    code_rows(tab: ndarray, k: int) -> np.ndarray

    The stabilizer block comes first so that the first n - k columns of the product matrix are the stabilizer syndromes and the last 2k the logical commutation pattern.

    autoqec_sim.ldpc ¶

    LDPC sparsity of a stabilizer group, batched over tableaux.

    Two quantities of a stabilizer group S with m = n - k generators:

    w* (minimum bottleneck weight) The smallest w such that the elements of S of weight at most w generate S; equivalently the smallest possible maximum generator weight over all generating sets. For m <= exact_max_generators (default 14) it is computed exactly: all 2^m group elements are enumerated as bit-packed uint64 rows, sorted by weight, and a batched GF(2) elimination gives the rank of the elements of weight <= w. The pivot rows of that elimination, restricted to weight <= w*, are a generating set with maximum weight w* (the sparsest basis reported here; it is a minimum-bottleneck basis, not necessarily a minimum-total-weight one). For larger m the fallback is a greedy pairwise reduction of the given generators (replace g_i by g_i g_j whenever that lowers its weight, to convergence); its maximum weight is an upper bound on w*.

    deg (maximum qubit degree) The largest number of generators of the sparsest basis acting on one qubit. The degree depends on the basis; the value reported is that of the basis above, so it is an upper bound on the minimum achievable maximum degree at bottleneck weight w*.

    The exact path costs O(2^m) memory per batch element and 2n vectorized elimination steps; at n = 9 and batch 512 one call takes a few milliseconds, cheap enough to run every environment step. Bit packing needs 2n <= 64.

    LdpcObjective combines the Knill-Laflamme term, the padding penalty, and the sparsity constraint into the reward and the success criterion of an LDPC-constrained [[n, k, d]] target, in one of the forms of LDPC_FORMS (compared at n = 12 and 16 in experiments/ldpc_scaling/REPORT.md; DEFAULT_LDPC_FORM is the one that comparison selected; the shaped and terminal forms and greedy_action_mask are the sparsity variants of experiments/ldpc_sparsity/REPORT.md; its "exact" method, the feasibility test after every two-qubit action on the pairs the greedy bound rejects, is the exact-mask section of that report).

    ExactMaskCache ¶

    Bounded cache of the light group elements of a stabilizer group for greedy_action_mask with method="exact", keyed by the bytes of the packed greedy basis (the same tableau gives the same basis, so a state seen again, such as the initial state after a reset, is not enumerated twice). Oldest entries are evicted above maxsize.

    LdpcObjective ¶

    Reward f(tab, k) -> (batch,) and success criterion success(tab, k, state_reward) -> (batch,) bool of an LDPC-constrained [[n, k, d]] target with bottleneck bound w_max (and optionally a qubit-degree bound deg_max).

    Base terms on every state: the Knill-Laflamme term over the Paulis of weight below d (autoqec_sim.reward.kl_reward) and the padding penalty (autoqec_sim.reward.low_weight_stabilizer_penalty at weight 1). A candidate is a state with every error detected and no idle qubit. Forms:

    "penalty" The rediscovery regression's form: normalized base (fraction of undetected errors, fraction of weight-1 Paulis in S) plus -scale * excess on every state. Success iff the reward is 0. At n >= 12 one undetected error is worth 1/630 to 1/1128 against scale = 0.25 per unit of w* excess, and PPO converges to sparse groups of distance 1 (experiments/scaling/REPORT.md). "unnormalized" Per-error base: the number of undetected errors and the number of weight-1 stabilizers, one unit each, plus -scale * excess, so that one undetected error costs 1 / scale units of w* excess. The sum is divided by r0, the number of undetected errors of the initial state (|0> ancillas, bare logical qubits), a global constant that keeps the reward within about [-1, 0] for the value head and changes neither the optimum nor the normalized-advantage policy gradient. Success iff the reward is 0. "final" Normalized base only; the constraint is hard and terminal: success iff the state is a candidate with exact w* <= w_max. No sparsity signal on the trajectory. "schedule" Distance first. Normalized base until activate is called (the trainer does so once the success rate at the target distance exceeds a threshold); from then on the penalty form. Before activation success is any candidate, after it the reward must be 0. "shaped" The unnormalized base divided by r0 minus shaping * excess in reward units on every state (greedy bound on ordinary states, exact on candidates), so that one unit of w* excess costs shaping * r0 undetected errors (3.75 to 15 at [[12, 2]] for shaping 0.05 to 0.2, against 0.25 in the unnormalized form). Success iff the reward is 0. "terminal" Count-unit terminal signal. Ordinary states get the unnormalized base divided by r0 and no sparsity term; a candidate ends the episode with reward 1 - h / m, where h is the number of generators of the sparsest basis with weight above w_max (heavy_generator_count, exact) and m = n - k, so one excess generator costs one unit out of m and a feasible code scores 1. Success (episode end) is any candidate; feasibility is h = 0, which feasible and the experiment check.

    Cost. On ordinary states w* is the greedy pairwise-reduction bound of this module (a few ms per batch; equal to the exact value on 95 to 99 percent of random states); on candidate states the exact w* replaces it (2^(n - k) group elements, exact_generators at most), where it decides success. last holds the terms of the last evaluated batch for diagnostics.

    heavy_generator_count ¶

    heavy_generator_count(
    tab: ndarray,
    k: int,
    w_max: int,
    exact_max_generators: int = EXACT_MAX_GENERATORS,
) -> np.ndarray

    (B,) number of generators of the sparsest basis with weight above w_max: m minus the rank of the group elements of weight at most w_max. Zero iff the group is feasible under w_max. Basis independent, since every bottleneck basis built lightest first contains exactly a basis of the light span. Exact for m <= exact_max_generators; for larger m the count of heavy rows of the greedy basis (an upper bound).

    greedy_action_mask ¶

    greedy_action_mask(
    tab: ndarray,
    k: int,
    action_table,
    w_max: int,
    method: str = "basis",
    exact_max_generators: int = EXACT_MAX_GENERATORS,
    cache: ExactMaskCache | None = None,
    stats: dict | None = None,
    chunk_rows: int = 1 << 22,
) -> np.ndarray

    (B, num_actions) bool: false where the action would take the stabilizer group outside the bound w* <= w_max. Single-qubit gates never change the support of a stabilizer, so they are always allowed. Three methods; the first two are upper bounds on w* (the mask can forbid an action whose exact w* is within the bound; it never allows one outside), the third is exact:

    "tableau" every two-qubit action is applied to a copy of the whole tableau batch and _greedy_stats runs from the tableau's generators on all copies in one call (0.13 s for 132 CNOT actions at n = 12, batch 256; 7 s for 600 at n = 25, most of it the copies and the packing). The method of the runs of experiments/ldpc_sparsity/REPORT.md at n = 12. "basis" the current state's greedy basis is computed once ((B, m) packed rows), every CNOT is applied to those packed rows with two bit operations (_packed_cnot), and _greedy_within re-reduces only the rows the gate made heavy (a CNOT raises the weight of a Pauli by at most one). No tableau copies; the cost scales with the number of heavy rows. Requires the two-qubit actions to be CNOTs (falls back to "tableau" otherwise). "exact" the "basis" bound as a pre-filter, then the exact feasibility test on every (state, action) pair the bound rejected: the group after the gate has a generating set within w_max iff the elements the gate leaves at weight <= w_max have rank m = n - k, decided by _exact_cnot_admits over the elements of weight <= w_max + 1 of the current group (the only ones a CNOT can bring within the bound), enumerated once per state and shared by all its actions (cache keeps them across calls for states seen again); the rank test is over the heavy rows of the gate-transformed basis only, since the light rows are in the light span already. Needs m <= exact_max_generators; above that the method is "basis" (stats["method"] records which ran). Two-qubit gates other than CNOT are tested exactly on tableau copies of the rejected pairs (ldpc_feasible).

    stats, when given, receives the counts of the call: two-qubit pairs, pairs the greedy bound rejected, pairs tested exactly (and how many of them were distinct, since identical states in the batch share one test per action), pairs the exact test admitted, cache hits and misses, and the seconds spent in the greedy and the exact parts.

    autoqec_sim.circuit_noise ¶

    Circuit-level noise for the reward, wired to autoqec_sim.noise.

    A noise model is any callable stim.Circuit -> stim.Circuit that inserts Pauli noise into a noiseless encoding circuit. Three forms are accepted wherever a noise model is expected (see resolve_noise_model):

    • a autoqec_sim.noise.Profile (presets.board(), presets.chain(), presets.forte(), presets.heron(), presets.depolarizing(p), or a variant built with with_bias, with_timing, with_params), applied through autoqec_sim.noise.noisifier(profile, scale);
    • a preset name ("board-rfc0001", "chain-2606.06455", "forte-2308.05071", "heron-r2");
    • a plain callable, such as the placeholder depolarizing_noise_model, which is kept for tests and as the profile-free fallback.

    The encoding circuit handed to the noise model is the gate list laid out in the TICK-layer convention of the noise module (gates_to_layered_circuit, as-soon-as-possible scheduling: a gate joins the earliest layer after the last gate on any of its qubits). The profile's timing model then decides how a layer maps onto time slots (parallel, sequential, or k two-qubit gates per slot), and its idle channel is charged to every qubit not operated in a slot. The profile's connectivity graph, when present, is the environment's graph (Graph.to_topology); a two-qubit gate on a non-edge makes the noise module raise ConnectivityError.

    The reward enumerates every fault mechanism of the noisy circuit (each Pauli term of each noise instruction with its probability, the same mechanism set that stim's detector-error-model derivation walks, before merging by detector signature), propagates the mechanism through the remaining gates (a GF(2) product against the symplectic map of the circuit suffix; fault_set_reference does the same with stim's PauliString.after and is kept as the cross-check), and scores the resulting Pauli on the encoded state with the batched Knill-Laflamme kernel. Heralded mechanisms (HERALDED_ERASE) count as detected. The reward is -sum_f p_f K_f over mechanisms, divided by sum_f p_f when normalized. A detector-error-model derivation of the same undetected mass is provided for cross-checks (dem_undetected_mass); it is not used in the reward because an encoding circuit has no detectors of its own and the logical X and Z readouts needed to see both kinds of logical fault anticommute, so they need two circuits.

    FaultSet dataclass ¶

    Propagated single-fault mechanisms of a noisy encoding circuit.

    paulis is (M, 2n) (the fault as a Pauli on the output state), probs is (M,), heralded is (M,) bool (mechanisms whose occurrence is flagged in the circuit and count as detected), and source is (M,) the index of the noise instruction in the flattened noisy circuit. Unpacks as paulis, probs.

    gates_to_layered_circuit ¶

    gates_to_layered_circuit(gates, n: int) -> stim.Circuit

    (gate, q1, q2) list as a TICK-layered noiseless skeleton on n qubits. As-soon-as-possible scheduling: each gate goes into the first layer after the last layer that touched one of its qubits. A QUBIT_COORDS line per qubit fixes num_qubits = n so that idle channels reach qubits the circuit never touches. The circuit is built from its text form in one parse (an order of magnitude faster than appending instruction by instruction).

    Propagate every single fault of noisy_circuit to the end.

    autoqec_sim.memory_objective ¶

    Multi-round memory objective: score a stabilizer code by the logical error rate of a syndrome-extraction memory experiment, not by its encoder.

    The encoder single-fault objective of autoqec_sim.circuit_noise cannot see a local-Clifford deformation of a code (a Hadamard at the end of the encoder only relabels weight-1 faults, all detected), so it cannot express bias tailoring (experiments/noise_aware/REPORT.md, verdict items 2 to 4 and 6). This module builds, for a code given by its stabilizer generators and logicals, an R-round syndrome-extraction circuit with one ancilla per generator, applies a autoqec_sim.noise.Profile with its timing model, derives stim's detector error model, and estimates the logical error rate per round with one of four fidelity tiers:

    proxy closed form from the DEM: the failure probability of the maximum-likelihood decoder restricted to fault sets of weight at most two (pfail_low_weight, O(M^2) in the number M of DEM mechanisms, exact to O(p^3)), plus the exact circuit-level distance d_circ up to weight 4 and the mass of its minimum-weight undetectable logical fault sets (exact_dcirc, ported from ion-search/lib.py). When no undetectable logical fault set of weight at most 4 exists (a circuit distance of 5 or 6) the weight-2 form is zero and the proxy escalates to weight 3: undetectable_logicals lists every weight-5 and weight-6 undetectable logical fault set by a canonical cluster search over the detector hypergraph, and their 3-subsets are the only weight-3 fault sets the decoder can get wrong. No sampling, no decoder dependency. sampled small-shot Monte Carlo from the DEM with an exact maximum-likelihood decoder when detectors + observables <= exact_ml_bits (dynamic program over the joint syndrome distribution, 2^(D+O) table; the decoder's failure probability is then exact and no shots are needed), otherwise a lookup decoder built from the same weight-<= 2 fault sets with a one-mechanism completion for unseen syndromes. bposd full sampling with the board's pinned BP+OSD decoder (ldpc, optional dependency, validation only). tesseract full sampling with Tesseract (tesseract-decoder, optional dependency), a most-likely-error search decoder that takes the DEM as it is, without decomposition; distinct syndromes are decoded once.

    undetectable_sets lists the minimum-weight undetectable logical fault sets of a DEM by probability (pair tables up to weight 3, the cluster search beyond), for the fault report of autoqec_sim.evaluate_code.

    Circuits (build_memory_circuit). Every generator g_j gets an ancilla prepared in |+>, controlled-P gates (CX, CY, CZ) onto its support in a fixed order, then H and a Z-basis measurement. By default every generator runs in one interleaved block with one measurement per round: the gate orders are chosen jointly among the hook-safe ones (hook_orders) and each generator's gates take layers inside a round as short as the longest generator allows, such that no qubit sees two gates in one layer and, for every pair of generators that share qubits with different Pauli letters, an even number of those qubits sees one generator first (otherwise an ancilla would measure its generator times Z of another ancilla, a random outcome). The standard four-layer surface-code cycle is one such schedule. When no schedule exists within the search cap (the Steane code), the generators fall back to batches of mutually interleavable ones, one block after another with their own measurements (extraction="batched" forces this). A autoqec_sim.code.SubsystemCode is measured through its gauge generators, in batches, and each stabilizer's detector compares the parity of the gauge outcomes whose product it is. Preparation and final readout are noiseless MPP measurements of every generator and of the logical operators of the chosen basis (Z or X memory); detectors compare consecutive measurements of each generator, and the observables compare the initial and final logical readout. With flags="one" each generator of weight at least three gets a flag qubit (|0>, two CX from the ancilla around the middle of the support, measured and declared a detector) in the Chao-Reichardt pattern; flags need all-to-all connectivity here.

    Connectivity (Layout). all_to_all_layout (the ion chain) places ancilla j on qubit n + j. square_layout(rows, cols) puts the data qubits on the lattice and ancilla sites at every plaquette center including the boundary ring, with edges only between a site and its corner data qubits (the rotated-surface-code hardware layout); generators are assigned to sites by a greedy minimum of the path lengths to their support, and a controlled gate to a non-adjacent qubit is routed along a shortest path with the nearest-neighbour CNOT ladder of the noise-aware experiment (intermediate qubits restored), so non-local generators pay in gates and depth. A generator that needs routing runs in a batch of its own. The profile's connectivity graph is replaced by the layout's graph, so the noise module's placement check applies to the routed circuit.

    Reward (MemoryReward). The environment reward of the noise-aware experiment with the memory term in place of the encoder term: min(d, d*)/d* - 1 - q_1 on every state and, on states at the target distance with no weight-1 stabilizer, weight * log10(p_ref / p_round) clipped to +-clip decades, where p_round is the per-round logical error estimate of the chosen tier summed over the memory bases. Such a state ends the episode (the reward exposes success_fn, which autoqec_sim.env.CodeDiscoveryEnv picks up). Results are cached by the reduced row echelon form of the stabilizer block, so a code is evaluated once per run. The memory term depends only on the code, not on the encoding circuit that produced it.

    code_distance(code: StabilizerCode | SubsystemCode) -> int

    hook_orders ¶

    hook_orders(
    code: StabilizerCode | SubsystemCode,
    target: int | None = None,
    seed: int = 0,
    interleave: bool = True,
    flags: str = "none",
) -> list[list[tuple[int, str]]]

    Hook-aware gate orders of every measured generator (_hook_order); target defaults to code_distance. With interleave the orders are chosen jointly, among the hook-safe ones, so that every generator can run in one interleaved block with one measurement per round (interleavable); when no such choice exists within the search cap, each generator gets its first hook-safe order and the circuit falls back to batches. flags is the flag variant the circuit will use, which shifts the gate layers of the flagged generators. A subsystem code's measured generators are its gauge generators, ordered against its gauge-fixed stabilizer code and never interleaved.

    pfail_low_weight ¶

    pfail_low_weight(
    sig: Signature,
    max_weight: int | None = 2,
    max_triples: int = 2000000,
    exclusive: bool = False,
) -> float

    Leading-order failure probability of the maximum-likelihood decoder restricted to fault sets of weight at most max_weight.

    Sets are grouped by syndrome, the decoder picks the observable pattern of largest summed weight per syndrome, and the rest fails. This is the leading term of the failure rate of a code whose circuit-level distance is at most 2 max_weight, meaningful while the expected number of faults per shot (sig.probs.sum()) is below about one.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    sig Signature

    Signature of the detector error model.

    		 required
    max_weight int | None

    2; 3 by enumeration of every triple when their number is at most max_triples, else through undetectable_logicals when no undetectable logical fault set of weight at most 4 exists (the 3-subsets of the weight-5 and weight-6 sets are then the only triples the decoder can get wrong), else 2; or None for 2 with that escalation to 3 whenever the weight-2 form is zero.

    		 2
    max_triples int

    Cap on the enumeration of every triple.

    		 2000000
    exclusive bool

    Weight a set by the exact probability of that set alone, prod p_i prod_{j not in set} (1 - p_j), instead of the low-p asymptote prod_{i in set} p_i.

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    float

    undetectable_logicals ¶

    undetectable_logicals(
    sig: Signature, wmax: int, chunk: int = 64
) -> dict[int, tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]

    Every irreducible undetectable logical fault set of a DEM with at most wmax mechanisms.

    A set of mechanisms is undetectable when their combined effect flips no detector, logical when it flips some observable, and irreducible when no proper nonempty subset is undetectable. The minimum-weight logical sets are irreducible, and so is every logical set lighter than min(d_circ + 3, 2 d_circ); in particular, at a circuit distance of 5 or 6, every weight-5 and weight-6 logical set.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    sig Signature

    Signature of the detector error model (fewer than 2**21 mechanisms).

    		 required
    wmax int

    Largest weight listed. The search visits about M (c / 2)^(wmax - 3) states for M mechanisms and a typical detector degree c: the 2,107-mechanism DEM of the 5x5 surface code at five rounds takes about two seconds at wmax = 5 and ten to twenty seconds at wmax = 6 (2.3e7 states).

    		 required
    chunk int

    Starting mechanisms processed together (memory against speed).

    		 64

    Returns:

    Type Description
    dict

    {weight: (sets, probabilities)} for every weight present, the sets as sorted (N, weight) arrays of mechanism indices and the probabilities their products of mechanism probabilities. Results are cached per DEM for the last few signatures.

    exact_dcirc ¶

    exact_dcirc(sig: Signature, wmax: int = 4) -> dict

    Exact circuit-level distance of a DEM up to wmax.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    sig Signature

    Signature of the detector error model; detector signatures wider than 64 bits are mapped to integer ids first.

    		 required
    wmax int

    Largest fault-set weight searched. Weights up to 4 come from the pair table; beyond, undetectable_logicals searches weight by weight, at a cost that grows about twentyfold per weight (6 is practical for a few thousand mechanisms).

    		 4

    Returns:

    Type Description
    dict

    d_circ (the smallest number of mechanisms whose combined effect flips no detector and some observable, None when no such set of weight <= wmax exists), count of such minimum-weight sets, mass (their summed probability product), and witness (one set as mechanism indices; the most probable beyond weight 4).

    undetectable_sets ¶

    undetectable_sets(
    sig: Signature,
    wmax: int = 3,
    limit: int = 10,
    chunk: int = 1000000,
) -> dict

    The minimum-weight undetectable logical fault sets of a DEM up to weight wmax, listed by probability: the smallest w such that some w mechanisms together flip no detector and some observable, the number of such sets, and the limit most probable of them as (mechanism indices, probability product) pairs in decreasing probability. weight is None and the list empty when no set of weight <= wmax exists. The weight is the d_circ of exact_dcirc whenever that is at most wmax; the count agrees with it. Triples are found as a pair plus a single with the pair's detector signature, scanned chunk pairs at a time; heavier sets come from undetectable_logicals, weight by weight.

    exact_ml_failure ¶

    exact_ml_failure(
    sig: Signature, max_bits: int = 20
) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray]

    Exact failure probability of the optimal (degenerate maximum likelihood) decoder for a DEM with D + O <= max_bits, by the dynamic program P <- (1 - p_i) P + p_i P[index xor v_i] over the joint distribution of (syndrome, observable flips) (the construction of ion-search/decoder/exact_decoder.py). Returns (p_fail, table) with table of shape (2^O, 2^D). The decision for syndrome s is argmax_o table[o, s]; p_fail = 1 - sum_s max_o table[o, s].

    per_round ¶

    per_round(p_shot: float, rounds: int) -> float

    Per-round logical error from the failure probability p of an R-round memory experiment, in the convention of the hardware memory experiments: (1 - (1 - 2p)^(1/R)) / 2, the per-round flip probability of a logical bit that can flip back, so that p saturates at one half. Agrees with 1 - (1 - p)^(1/R) to first order in p.

    autoqec_sim.evaluate ¶

    One-call evaluation of a stabilizer code under a device noise profile.

    evaluate_code builds the R-round memory experiment of autoqec_sim.memory_objective in both bases, applies the profile, and returns a CodeEvaluation: the logical error per round of the chosen tier summed over the bases, the per-basis dictionaries, the exact circuit-level distance and the mass of its minimum-weight undetectable fault sets per basis (computed from the detector error model whatever the tier), and the most probable minimum-weight undetectable fault sets explained back to circuit locations with stim's explain_detector_error_model_errors.

    FaultLocation dataclass ¶

    One DEM mechanism as a circuit error: the noise instruction gate (stim name, such as DEPOLARIZE2 or M), its qubits, the pauli product it flips ("Y10", "Z10*X7", or "flip Z9" for a measurement flip), the number of TICK layers before it, and the DEM targets it produces ("D1 D4 L0"). gate is "?" when stim cannot attribute the mechanism to one circuit error.

    DominantFault dataclass ¶

    A minimum-weight undetectable logical fault set of one basis: the DEM mechanism indices (into dem.flattened() error instructions), the product of their probabilities, and one circuit location per mechanism.

    CodeEvaluation dataclass ¶

    Result of evaluate_code.

    p_round is the per-round logical error of tier summed over the bases; per_basis maps each basis to the dictionary of MemoryObjective.score_basis with d_circ, d_circ_count, and d_circ_mass added; d_circ and d_circ_mass repeat the exact circuit-level distance (None above 6) and the summed probability product of its minimum-weight undetectable fault sets per basis; dominant_faults holds the most probable such sets over both bases, most probable first (empty for a basis whose d_circ is 7 or more).

    explain_mechanisms ¶

    explain_mechanisms(
    circuit: Circuit, dem: DetectorErrorModel, indices
) -> dict[int, FaultLocation]

    One circuit error per DEM mechanism: indices into the error instructions of dem.flattened() (the mechanism order of autoqec_sim.memory_objective.dem_signature), explained on the noisy circuit the DEM came from with explain_detector_error_model_errors. A mechanism stim cannot attribute to a single circuit error gets gate="?".
